Upon discharge, the patient was scheduled for outpatient monitoring by an endocrinologist and advised to continue her oncological regimen without modifications.

clinician.final_diagnosis: thyrotoxicosis episode due to autoimmune thyroiditis, secondary to immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old female with pleural mesothelioma on nivolumab and ipilimumab presented with progressive neurocognitive symptoms suggesting delirium. Thyroid function tests revealed elevated total T4 and T3 levels, negative TRAb and TPO antibodies, and positive anti-thyroglobulin antibodies, consistent with autoimmune thyroiditis. Thyroid iodine uptake was low, supporting thyroiditis as the cause of thyrotoxicosis. Symptomatic beta-blocker treatment led to gradual neurological improvement. This sequence confirms thyrotoxicosis from autoimmune thyroiditis triggered by immunotherapy as the delirium etiology.
